## What a user of the old system will notice

**Ticket closing will feel the same when it works, and much better when SMTP is having a bad
day** (ED-001, PB-001) — the response no longer waits on an email send that can take up to 30
seconds under provider trouble. Nothing about the *content* of that notification changes: same
fixed recipient (`watchers@example.internal`), same message text. Requesting a password reset
gets the identical treatment (ED-001b) — same email content, just dispatched off the request path.

**Password resets will feel identical from the outside, but the token itself is no longer a
security liability** (ED-002, PB-002) — still expires in 30 minutes, still single-use, still
returns the exact same error for an expired token as for one that never existed (that
non-disclosure behavior is FIXED, not touched). What changes is invisible to any caller: no more
MD5, no more raw tokens sitting in a bare table forever.

## What nobody will notice (because it's frozen, not fixed)

Every quirk the current UI relies on ships unchanged: a missing ticket still returns `200 {}`
instead of `404` (PB-007); `priority` still accepts `"1"`/`"2"`/`"3"` or the words interchangeably
(PB-006 forecloses cleaning this up); the ticket list still has no pagination and returns
everything every time. Two tickets with titles that normalize to the same slug — "Fix DB" and
"fix db!" — will still both succeed and both get slug `fix-db` (PB-003) until someone rules
**OQ-001** on what, if anything, should change about that.

## What's still genuinely undecided

The `X-Internal-Bypass` header that defeats reset-request rate limiting (PB-008) is neither being
carried forward nor removed until **OQ-002** is ruled — WO-004 ships with that one code path as a
documented gap rather than guessing. Three more open questions (**OQ-006** naive vs. UTC-aware
timestamps, **OQ-009** what timezone legacy actually ran in, **OQ-010** whether to migrate old
reset-token rows at all) gate WO-005's data migration from fully closing. See `decisions.md` for
the complete list.
